All changes are in place and the production build passes. Here's a summary of what I did.

## What changed

Dependency upgrade: React/react-dom 19.1.0 → 19.3.0. The <ViewTransition> component and addTransitionType API that power these transitions are only exported at runtime starting in React 19.3 (the types were already forward-declared in 19.1, but the runtime export was undefined). Next.js 16 canary's peer range ^19.0.0 accepts 19.3.0.

### 1. Shared element morph (thumbnail → hero image)
- app/ProductGrid.tsx: each grid thumbnail is wrapped in <ViewTransition name={product-image-${slug}} share="morph" default="none">.
- app/product/[slug]/page.tsx: the large hero image is wrapped in the matching <ViewTransition name>. React pairs the two elements by name and the browser morphs size/position automatically. share="morph" + default="none" lets the CSS add a mid-flight blur to hide interpolation artifacts and prevents the pair from crossfading on unrelated transitions.

### 2. Directional page slides (forward / back)
- Grid <Link>s carry transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}; the back link carries transitionTypes={['nav-back']}.
- Both app/page.tsx and the product page wrap their main content in a <ViewTransition> whose enter/exit props map nav-forward → slide-left and nav-back → slide-right, with default: 'none' so untyped navigations (browser back/forward, refresh) don't slide. The wrapper is in each page.tsx, not the layout, because layouts persist across navigations and enter/exit never fire there.
- CSS in globals.css defines ::view-transition-old/new(.nav-forward) and .nav-back with asymmetric timing (old leaves fast at 150ms, new enters gently at 210ms delayed until the exit finishes, slide movement runs 400ms).

### 3. Suspense loading-state transition (skeleton → content)
- The product detail page's DetailsSkeleton fallback is wrapped in <ViewTransition exit="slide-down" default="none"> and the real ProductDetails content in <ViewTransition enter="slide-up" default="none">. The skeleton slides down/fades out, then the content slides up/fades in. Same pattern is available to the grid's Suspense boundary.

### 4. Reduced motion
- globals.css ends with a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block that forces animation-duration: 0s and animation-delay: 0s on all ::view-transition-old/new/group(), so every transition collapses to an instant swap.

### Supporting CSS
- ::view-transition { pointer-events: none; } lets clicks pass through the transition overlay to the live page during animations.
- Duration custom properties (--duration-exit/enter/move) and the fade, slide-y, slide, via-blur keyframes were added per the Next.js view-transitions guide.

Verification: npm run build completed successfully — compiled, TypeScript passed, all 3 routes generated. The patterns follow the Next.js 16 dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/view-transitions.md guide and were checked against the installed @types/react and next/dist/client/link.d.ts API surfaces.

One note: view transitions require Chromium 125+ (and recent Safari/Firefox). In unsupported browsers the app works normally with instant swaps — no degradation or errors.
